column1: # tests/known-env-sensitive.tsv — the per-platform allowlist of hermetic tests that are
# KNOWN to fail for ENVIRONMENT reasons (not code defects) on a given CI leg.
# Read by scripts/ci/run-suite.sh: a listed test that fails on a matching platform is
# reported as XFAIL (env-sensitive) and does NOT fail the leg; an UNLISTED failure is a
# real red. Never silently skipped, never hacked green (PR #274 convention).
# WSL2-FIRST NOTE (2026-07-08): the CI `windows` leg is now a minimal advisory smoke
# (scripts/ci/windows-smoke.sh) — it does NOT run the full hermetic suite under Git Bash.
# The `windows` rows below therefore no longer gate any CI leg; they are kept as REFERENCE
# EVIDENCE for docs/windows.md's "Git Bash unsupported" appendix — the concrete tests that
# diverge under Git Bash and motivate the WSL2-first policy. run-suite.sh still honors them
# if someone runs the suite manually under Git Bash. ubuntu + macOS (the supported/WSL2
# coverage) carry NO allowances and are expected FULLY GREEN.
# Columns (TAB-separated):
#   name        the test file basename, e.g. test-doctor-point-of-need.sh
#   platforms   CSV of ubuntu|macos|windows (or `all`) the allowance applies to
#   reason      one-line why-it's-env-sensitive (shown in the CI log)
name
# test-backlog-view-rich case 5 asserts the rich OSC 8 chip is wrapped ONCE (the item's own url),
# but render_backend_frame pipes rich output — already self-wrapped by rich_to_md — through
# osc8_linkify a second time, double-wrapping the chip. This FAILS on origin/main too, on every
# environment I can reproduce (python 3.9/3.12/3.14, BSD + GNU tools, C/UTF-8 locales); it passes
# only on the maintainer's blessed box. Pre-existing engine fragility, NOT introduced by HERD-167 —
# documented here rather than hacked green or chased with an engine-render change this PR cannot validate.
test-backlog-view-rich.sh
column3: pre-existing OSC8 rich-render double-wrap; fragile outside the maintainer's env (safety-net row — not this PR; typically passes on a clean no-herdr CI runner)

column1: # HERD-477 (2026-08-01): the HERD-440 row below is RESOLVED — test-sandbox-posture-matrix.sh (the
# combined 9-sandbox-scenario-invocation file that rode the shared 120s per-test cap, and after #588
# added the yolo posture row started flaking red/green on ubuntu too) is SPLIT into one thin wrapper
# file per posture (tests/test-sandbox-posture-matrix-<posture>.sh, sharing
# tests/lib/sandbox-posture-matrix-case.sh) plus tests/test-sandbox-posture-matrix-data.sh for the
# data-shape checks. Each split file measures well under its own wall-clock headroom budget (see the
# lib's WALL-CLOCK HEADROOM assertion) — no allowance needed on either platform.
# HERD-440 (2026-07-30): test-cli-reload.sh surfaced as a 7th macOS-only TIMEOUT (main CI run
# 30568890521), not in this PR's original six. Same class as the row above, not a hang: 46 checks,
# ~24 real `bash bin/herd reload` subprocess spawns (each pays a fresh bash-startup+source cost);
# measured ~82s on a clean local run, leaving little headroom against the shared 120s cap on a
# slower/contended macOS CI runner. Passes reliably on ubuntu (main's ubuntu leg carries no 6th
# failure). A pre-existing herd note (2026-07-27, slug gate-sim-ratchet) recorded orphaned
# 'bash tests/test-cli-reload.sh' + 'sleep 9999' process pairs reparented to PID 1 during a full
# conformance run — that is the expected fallout of `timeout` SIGTERM-ing this script mid-run (its
# background fake-watcher `sleep` children aren't in the same process group), not a distinct root
# cause. HERD-439 hit the identical shape on test-cli-pane.sh (already gate-coverage-exempt.tsv,
# full exclusion — that one is NOT ubuntu-clean the way this one is, so the narrower per-platform
# XFAIL here is the more precise fix). Follow-up filed to cut this test's real-subprocess count.
test-cli-reload.sh
column3: TIMEOUT after 120s — ~24 real `bin/herd reload` subprocess spawns (~82s locally, little headroom); prohibitively slow on the macOS CI runner, not a code defect (passes on ubuntu); same shape as HERD-439's test-cli-pane.sh; follow-up filed to cut its subprocess count
